Release Phase 8 builds the tag with a bare `./build.ps1` (.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md:140-142). TAOM: 47 NPCCharacters files, 7,722,487 bytes, plus lords.xslt (1,515,721 bytes, 397 NPCCharacter[@id] templates; SubModule.xml:118-120) and heroes.xslt (177,579 bytes, 397 templates; :128-130). EquipmentRosters: 28 files, 1,890,380 bytes. GameText: 16 files, 1,580,909 bytes. 8 XSLTs total 1,941,350 bytes; 409 ModuleData XML files total 37,485,381 bytes (12 languages included). items.symbol: Patch59_CaravanTrade: GetTradeScoreForTown, CanTradeWith, GetDistanceLimitVeryFarAsDaysForNavigationType and CalculateBudgetFactor postfixes
items.hook: Harmony postfixes on private CaravansCampaignBehavior methods (applied SubModule.cs:574-578)
items.frequency: per caravan destination search: 78 towns x (CanTradeWith + GetTradeScoreForTown + several VeryFar getter calls) x up to 2 passes; 302 caravans at +30 s on a new campaign (map-load-diagnostics.md:31)
items.evidence: Vanilla ThinkNextDestination runs FindNextDestinationForCaravan twice when the first pass finds nothing (E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord/_shipping_build/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.cs:178046-178053). Each pass loops Town.AllTowns, calling CanTradeWith and GetTradeScoreForTown (178057-178085). The patched VeryFar getter is also reached through the Close/Medium/Far wrappers inside AdjustVeryFarAddition (177406-177416) and directly at 178089, 178121 and 178130. The TAOM GetTradeScoreForTown postfix repeats AiHelper.GetBestNavigationTypeAndAdjustedDistanceOfSettlementForMobileParty (patch :40-41), which vanilla just ran at 178114, then does a visit-memory lookup (:55) and a Math.Pow reweight (CaravanTradeService.cs:25-60). The VeryFar postfix reads Enabled and RangeMultiplier (CaravanTradeService.cs:70-76), each a TaomSettings.Instance read (CaravanTradeSettingsProvider.cs:21, 23). CanTradeWith runs IsAtWarWith plus a string-keyed policy on every war-vetoed pair (:31-56). 78 towns = 221 <Town minus 143 is_castle in TAOM_Map/ModuleData/settlements.xml. The lifted war veto and wider range mean fewer early -1 exits and more full scoring loops (item roster x ItemCategories, 178142-178160) [inferred]. All four targets are shield-eligible, so each carries a PatchShield finalizer.
costPatterns: duplicate navigation-distance query per town per pass
2 MCM registry lookups per VeryFar call, several calls per score
more candidates fully scored than vanilla
items.suggestedLever: Capture vanilla's computed distance instead of recomputing it (prefix __state or a transpiler hand-off). Cache the TaomSettings reference in CaravanTradeSettingsProvider (the BattleBalanceSettingsProvider.cs:14-15 pattern). Count calls per in-game day on the [MapLoad] heartbeat.

items.symbol: TaomPartySpeedModel.CalculateFinalSpeed + Patch18 PartyBaseHelper_HasFeat_Patch (skip-original prefix) + Patch10 DefaultMapWeatherModel_GetWeatherEventInPosition_Patch
items.hook: GameModel override plus Harmony prefixes, reached from MobileParty.CalculateSpeedForPartyUnified
items.frequency: per moving party whenever its nav face, night state, prisoner state or wind changes; 2,091 parties at Stop, rising to 3,042 during fast-forward (docs/migration/v1.5.2-impact.md:146-147); more often per frame at the 8x/16x multipliers
items.evidence: Every tick ComputeNextMoveDistance calls CalculateSpeed (TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.cs:104738-104748), which recomputes CalculateFinalSpeed when IsLastSpeedCacheInvalid, for example on a nav-face index change (104996-105011, 105038-105075). Vanilla CalculateFinalSpeed calls PartyBaseHelper.HasFeat (67229, 67245) and GetWeatherEventInPosition (67257); the vanilla weather body is just an array read (64224-64228). TAOM replaces HasFeat with a prefix (PartyBaseHelper_HasFeat_Patch.cs:34-39 -> CultureFeatAdapter.cs:62-77) and clamps the weather position (DefaultMapWeatherModel_GetWeatherEventInPosition_Patch.cs:12-22). The override then walks the whole roster (TaomPartySpeedModel.cs:70-80), makes two feat calls and a career-passive lookup that takes a lock plus two dictionary lookups (CareerPassiveService.cs:110-133, 166-180). GetTerrainSize and GetFaceTerrainType are field reads (E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord/_modules_build/SandBox__SandBox.cs:1787-1791, 2053-2062), so TAOM's overhead is the detours, their shield finalizers and the roster walk [magnitude inferred].
costPatterns: roster walk on every speed recompute
2-4 Harmony detours with PatchShield finalizers per recompute
items.suggestedLever: Count mounted troops only when a Rohan-infantry feat can apply (culture check first). Add HasFeat and the three weather targets to PatchShieldPolicy.ExcludedTargetMethods, since they are pure lookups. Add a call counter to confirm frequency.

items.symbol: CultureMarketplaceBehavior.OnDailyTickSettlement -> EnsureGuaranteedStock / FilterForeignCultureItems / SelectItems / AddItem
items.hook: CampaignEvents.DailyTickSettlementEvent (:73)
items.frequency: per town per in-game day (78 towns; the event fires for all ~1,002 settlements and is rejected by IsTown at :148)

items.suggestedLever: Build the routed and pooled id sets once per culture in BuildPools; resolve ItemObjects once; count the roster once into a dictionary per town tick.

Many desktop timings in the docs were recorded in that slow mode.

MCM read cost: TaomSettings.Instance is GlobalSettings<T>.Instance, which does two ConcurrentDictionary operations plus a walk of the settings containers on every read (E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord/_modules_build/TAOM.Dependencies__MCMv5.cs:6321-6331, 2214-2233). About 100 per-read getters across 40 files remain uncached (deep-review-003-hot-path-resolve-and-grid-caching-2026-09-24.md:71, 154). One RCA calls it an 'O(1) cached lookup' (rca-ai-party-size-2026-08-18.md:17), which the decompile contradicts.

Logging: FileLogger writes INFO, WARNING and ERROR synchronously with a Flush on the calling (game) thread; DEBUG is queued but always formatted, with no level gate (FileLogger.cs:85-124; CareerPassiveService.cs:125-130).
summary:
I inventoried TAOM's campaign and load-time hot paths: the event listeners (8 TickEvent, 10 hourly, 12 daily global, plus per-entity DailyTickParty, DailyTickSettlement and DailyTickHero), the Harmony patches on AI, speed, caravan, text, gold and map-frame paths, the per-party GameModels, map rendering (RealmBorders, nameplates, map-bar mixins), and boot, XML, save and load costs. No TAOM behavior registers on HourlyTickPartyEvent, HourlyTickSettlementEvent, HourlyTickClanEvent or DailyTickClanEvent. Patch42 instead postfixes vanilla's per-party hourly RecruitmentCampaignBehavior.HourlyTickParty. No uncached IoC.Resolve appears on a campaign hot path. TAOM overrides no settlement-value or encounter model.

Ranked findings:
1. TAOM appears to ship a Debug-configuration DLL. build.ps1 defaults to Debug, the release skill builds with a bare ./build.ps1, and the deployed DLL's size matches the Debug output. This is a cheap, broad multiplier.
2. The engine's per-game-start XML merge and XSLT compile are amplified by TAOM's data shape: 47 NPCCharacters files, a 1.5 MB lords.xslt with 397 templates that is recompiled every start, and 131 Armory item-file merge steps. It is unmeasured but structurally quadratic.
3. PatchShield pass 2 runs at every game start: about 125 attaches on the first start after #651 and about 140 on a second start. That is about 1-3 s on players and tens of seconds on the desktop, and it plausibly explains the audit's 25.6 s and 67 s silent windows [inferred].
4. The caravan trade postfixes multiply the per-destination search: 78 towns, a duplicate distance query per town, several MCM-reading getter calls per score, and up to two passes, across 302+ caravans.
5. TaomPartySpeedModel plus the HasFeat and weather prefixes run on every speed recompute (each nav-face change) for 2,000-3,000 parties.
Medium items are the GetLocalizedText substring allocation per text, the unmeasured per-call PatchShield tax, the default-on AutoResolve battle log (synchronous flush per world battle), CultureMarketplace's O(routed x roster) daily town pass, Patch42's per-party MCM reads and extra castle candidates, RealmBorders' per-frame MCM reads with its 0.2-0.6 s parchment hitch and 3 ms/frame sampling, the uncached Morale/Food/Wage model re-runs, the per-save hero race map, boot reflection, and map-load data scale.

Already fixed: #651 (d90b4be3) and #650 (plan 006) for PatchShield and Native2Managed boot cost, #655 (ed1732eb) for the per-frame loading-window trace, #465 for the per-frame nameplate NRE, plus Patch38 settings caching and #331's Gauntlet exclusion.

Caveats:
- E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord/_manifest.json still says v1.4.8, but the _diff_1.5.2_to_1.5.3 headers show _shipping_build and _modules_build are v1.5.3. All engine line numbers come from those dumps.
- Many recorded timings (69 s pass 2, 7-8 fps fast-forward, 25.6 s/67 s load windows) come from the maintainer desktop's slow mode (117-190 ms per Harmony.Patch, likely the VS mixed-mode debugger), so they overstate player cost.
- No per-handler or LoadXML timing instrument exists.

Cheapest next measurements:
- A Release-vs-Debug A/B, and a patchshield-disabled.flag A/B, both against [MapLoad] tickMs/fps.
- Call counters on the caravan, speed and GetLocalizedText patches.
- A stamp around LoadXML.
Fitting skills: /investigate for root-causing a measured regression and /research for the engine side.
